topic: Text-to-SQL Generation with Large Language Models: Schema Linking, Benchmarks, and Robustness

per_sentence.text: Their survey also examines various schema linking and data augmentation techniques that have been proposed to enhance text-to-SQL approaches, situating these methods alongside supervised fine-tuning-based strategies that predate the current era of large language models (Câmara et al., 2024).

judge.rationale: The cited paper focuses on SQL-to-text generation using LLMs and does not examine schema linking, data augmentation, or supervised fine-tuning strategies for text-to-SQL, nor does it survey such techniques.

per_sentence.text: Large language models (LLMs) have enabled substantial progress in natural-language-to-SQL (NL2SQL) systems, which allow non-expert users to query relational databases through natural language questions (Câmara et al., 2024).

judge.rationale: The cited paper addresses SQL-to-text explanation, not natural-language-to-SQL (NL2SQL) systems, so it does not support the claim about LLMs enabling progress in NL2SQL.

per_sentence.text: Despite these advances, a critical bottleneck persists: accurately identifying which parts of the database schema are relevant to a given question—a process known as schema linking (Câmara et al., 2024).

judge.rationale: The cited paper discusses SQL-to-text generation using LLMs and does not address schema linking or the challenge of identifying relevant database schema parts for a question.

per_sentence.text: Their approach first generates a preliminary SQL query using the complete database schema and employs bidirectional schema linking to achieve a high recall rate, thereby reducing the risk of incomplete results (Câmara et al., 2024).

judge.rationale: The cited paper discusses SQL-to-text explanation generation using LLMs, but it does not describe a method that generates a preliminary SQL query using a complete database schema or employs bidirectional schema linking to achieve high recall.

per_sentence.text: Their work frames schema linking as a trade-off between positive gain and negative impact, and they propose a framework that first generates a preliminary SQL query using the complete schema, employing bidirectional schema linking to achieve high recall and reduce the risk of incomplete results (Câmara et al., 2024).

judge.rationale: The cited paper discusses SQL-to-text generation using LLMs and does not address schema linking, bidirectional schema linking, or the trade-off between positive gain and negative impact in SQL generation.
